title: Volume and Surface Area of Prisms and Cylinders
seo_title: Sec 1 Volume and surface area Worksheets: Free Secondary 1 Maths with Answers (MOE Syllabus)
standard_text: volume and surface area of prism and cylinder; conversion between cm² and m², and between cm³ and m³; problems involving volume and surface area of composite solids
meta_desc: Free Secondary 1 volume and surface area worksheets with diagrams: cuboids, triangular prisms, cylinders, surface area and capacity in litres. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Volume of a prism = area of cross-section × length.
key_sub: Surface area = total area of all the faces. 1000 cm³ = 1 litre.
body_html:
How it works

A prism has the same cross-section all the way through. Volume = area of cross-section × length. For a cuboid that is length × width × height; for a cylinder it is πr²h.

Surface area is the total area of all the faces. A cuboid has 6 faces in 3 matching pairs.

1 cm³ = 1 ml, so 1000 cm³ = 1 litre.

Example

Find the volume and surface area of the cuboid above.

V = 5 × 3 × 4 = 60 cm³.

SA = 2(15 + 12 + 20) = 94 cm².

Answer: 60 cm³ and 94 cm²

Example

A triangular prism has a right-angled triangle 6 cm by 8 cm and length 10 cm. Find its volume.

Cross-section = ½ × 6 × 8 = 24 cm².

24 × 10 = 240.

Answer: 240 cm³

Common mistakes

  • Adding the lengths instead of multiplying for volume.
  • Forgetting to halve when the cross-section is a triangle.
  • Counting only three faces of a cuboid for surface area (there are six).
  • Using the diameter in πr²h, or thinking 100 cm³ = 1 litre.

faq.q: How do I find the volume of a prism?
faq.a: Find the area of the cross-section (the shape that runs all the way through) and multiply by the length.

faq.q: What is the formula for the volume of a cylinder?
faq.a: V = πr²h: the area of the circle times the height.

faq.q: How do I find the surface area of a cuboid?
faq.a: Find the area of the three different faces, add them, and double: 2(lw + wh + lh).
